snapshot.business_model: Tata Consultancy Services is India's largest IT services firm, selling software development, consulting, cloud, and business-process outsourcing to enterprises worldwide. It earns through multi-year contracts billed by time-and-materials and fixed-price, with revenue concentrated in BFSI and North America. Its asset-light model throws off very high returns on capital and large free cash flow, most of which is returned to shareholders.
snapshot.stance_rationale: Best-in-class returns and cash generation, but decelerating growth and a rich multiple leave limited near-term upside.

business.summary: Revenue is led by BFSI and North America; growth tilts to Manufacturing and Energy while Communications & Media lags.

peers.note: TCS screens at the top of the Indian IT pack on returns and cash, at a premium multiple.

supports.text: Market leader in Indian IT services with deep, sticky enterprise relationships and a large, diversified deal pipeline.
Best-in-class returns (ROCE ~64%, ROE ~52%) and an asset-light, net-cash balance sheet.
Strong free cash flow conversion funds a consistent dividend plus periodic buybacks.
Healthy large-deal total contract value signed in FY25 supports forward revenue visibility.

counters.text: Discretionary technology spend remains soft, pressuring near-term revenue growth.
Revenue growth has decelerated toward high-single-digits from mid-teens.
Wage inflation and attrition can compress margins if pricing doesn't keep pace.
Valuation at ~29x earnings is rich relative to the current growth rate.

change_my_mind: Constant-currency revenue growth sustainably above 8% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
EBIT margin recovering above 26% on better utilization and pricing.
P/E de-rating below 22x, offering a more attractive entry.
A large, sustained step-up in AI-led deal wins translating into reported revenue.

insights: Demand is stabilising but not yet inflecting — growth is a FY26 H2 story.
The margin band (26–28%) is the key value driver; levers exist but need volume.
GenAI is additive to deals today, but a potential deflation risk to legacy work later.
Large-deal TCV gives revenue visibility despite soft discretionary spend.
Easing attrition and resumed campus hiring signal management confidence in the ramp.
concall.tone: Cautiously optimistic — guidance-light but reiterated the medium-term margin band.

mna.summary: Growth is overwhelmingly organic; inorganic activity is limited to occasional bolt-ons.

deals.what: Captive IT services unit of Deutsche Bank's Postbank
deals.rationale: Deepen European banking delivery; ~1,500 employees onboarded

estimates.summary: Street models high-single-digit revenue growth with gradual margin recovery; price targets span a wide range.
estimates.eps_revision: Marginal downgrades over the last quarter on soft discretionary demand.

risks.summary: The dominant risk is a prolonged discretionary-spend slowdown in the US/Europe; margins and FX are secondary.

register.evidence: ~66% of revenue from North America + UK; BFSI (31%) soft.
LTM attrition ~13%; supply tight in niche/AI skills.
GenAI can compress effort-based billing over time.
Onsite delivery depends on work visas.
